title: Coherent transport between dg functor models
statement: Use derived enrichment and enhanced localization of dg categories over $\mathbf Z$ as in [lem-coef-dg-enrichment-rectification], and coherent enriched internal Hom, evaluation, composition and identities as in [lem-coef-enriched-category-tensor-calculus]. Fix a small collection of small dg categories. For every ordered pair $(\mathcal A,\mathcal B)$ in the collection put $\mathcal F(\mathcal A,\mathcal B)=\operatorname{Fun}_{\mathbf D(\mathbf Z)}(\mathcal A,\mathcal B)$. Suppose two families of small dg models $\mathcal R_i(\mathcal A,\mathcal B)$, $i=1,2$, have specified enriched equivalences $e_i(\mathcal A,\mathcal B):\mathcal R_i(\mathcal A,\mathcal B)\simeq\mathcal F(\mathcal A,\mathcal B)$. The coherent evaluation, composition, identities and all their higher compatibility homotopies on $\mathcal F$ admit transport to each family along the $e_i$. For the transported structures the pairwise equivalences $e_2^{-1}e_1:\mathcal R_1(\mathcal A,\mathcal B)\simeq\mathcal R_2(\mathcal A,\mathcal B)$ respect these operations with all higher compatibility homotopies. They identify the derived transformation objects in $\mathbf D(\mathbf Z)$.

source.place: Haugseng, On the tensor product of enriched infinity-categories, Remark 9.5 and Corollary 10.8; transport of its coherent internal-Hom operations along enriched equivalences. Agent specialization, read online, not archived. No Stacks tag supplies this enriched coherence lemma.

proof.text: Regard every given dg model as a derived-chain-enriched category through [lem-coef-dg-enrichment-rectification]. Put $\mathcal M=\operatorname{Cat}_{\mathbf D(\mathbf Z)}$. By [lem-coef-enriched-category-tensor-calculus], $\mathcal M$ is closed symmetric monoidal and has the coherent internal-Hom operations in the hypothesis. Work in a containing universe in which its monoidal total category and the small collection in the statement are small. All indexing objects below consist of finite lists from that collection, so are small. Write $h_{AB}$ and $v_A$ for formal color labels, to be assigned $\mathcal F(A,B)$ and $A$ respectively.

source.place: Remark 9.5; derived-enrichment interpretation supplied by the cited rectification statement.

proof.text: Define an ordinary symmetric colored operad $O$ on the labels $h_{AB},v_A$. Its operations with hom output are ordered composable strings $(h_{A_{r-1}A_r},\ldots,h_{A_0A_1})\to h_{A_0A_r}$; the empty string at $A$ has output $h_{AA}$. Its operations with value output are $(h_{A_{r-1}A_r},\ldots,h_{A_0A_1},v_{A_0})\to v_{A_r}$, including $r=0$. Include every relabeling of the inputs, remembering the indicated ordering, and no other operations. Substitution replaces a hom slot by its string and replaces the unique value slot by a string ending in a value slot. Thus substitution is concatenation with matching endpoints; flattening a nested list in either order gives the same list. Singleton strings and $r=0$ value strings are unary identities. This verifies associativity, identities and permutation equivariance, including nullary hom operations. Use the category of operators $O^\otimes$ of [lem-coef-colored-operation-section-reconstruction], and put $B=N(O^\otimes)$. Its vertices are finite color tuples, including the empty tuple.

source.place: Construction 2.1.1.7; explicit path-and-action colored operad, with substitution verified by list concatenation.

proof.text: Let $\mathcal M^\otimes\to N(\mathrm{Fin}_*)$ present the symmetric monoidal structure of Step 1. Pull it back along the arity functor $B\to N(\mathrm{Fin}_*)$, obtaining $q:E^\otimes\to B$. The operad and relative-algebra conventions are [def-coef-relative-symmetric-operadic-algebras]. The pullback lifts inner horns and has cocartesian lifts by projecting a lifting problem to $\mathcal M^\otimes$ and pairing its filler with the specified base simplex. The same argument with the defining cocartesian horns preserves the chosen lifts. Its tuple fibers are $\mathcal M^r$ under inert projections; its operation transport is the ordered tensor of the inputs. Its mapping-space Segal decompositions are those of $\mathcal M^\otimes$ restricted to each operator of $O$. Hence it meets the hypotheses of [lem-coef-colored-operation-section-reconstruction]. Assign the colors $h_{AB}\mapsto\mathcal F(A,B)$, $v_A\mapsto A$; assign the hom-string operations iterated composition, the empty hom string the identity functor, and the value-string operations iterated evaluation. The coherent composition, evaluation and currying of [lem-coef-enriched-category-tensor-calculus] supply the tree-substitution data, with tensor symmetries for relabeled inputs. The reconstruction theorem gives an inert-preserving section $s:B\to E^\otimes$ realizing these data, with all their higher simplices.

source.place: Definition 2.1.3.1; reconstruction applied to the path-and-action operations. Haugseng Remark 9.5 provides the closed internal Hom through the existing tensor-calculus node.

proof.text: Fix $i\in\{1,2\}$. For each tuple $\mathbf c=(c_1,\ldots,c_r)$ choose an object $x_{i,\mathbf c}$ in its fiber corresponding to the tuple obtained by replacing $\mathcal F(A,B)$ by $\mathcal R_i(A,B)$ and retaining each $A$. Choose an equivalence $a_{i,\mathbf c}:x_{i,\mathbf c}\to s(\mathbf c)$ in that fiber whose singleton projections are the specified $e_i(A,B)$ and the identity of $A$, with the comparison identifications retained. The inert Segal equivalence in Step 3 supplies these choices: apply its inverse functor to the tuple of equivalences and its counit. At a singleton take exactly the specified object and edge. At the empty tuple the fiber is equivalent to a point and the same construction applies. These fiber equivalences are equivalences in $E^\otimes$, since fiber inclusion carries their inverse edges and triangles to inverse edges and triangles. No coherence between different tuples has yet been assumed.

source.place: Tuple-fiber Segal equivalences and inverse functors; preparation of the prescribed vertex data for the relative prism theorem.

proof.text: Let $A_0=\operatorname{sk}_0B$, the simplicial subset consisting of the vertices and their degeneracies. The edges $a_{i,\mathbf c}$ define a map $\Delta^1\times A_0\to E^\otimes$; on $\{1\}\times B$ use $s$. These agree on $\{1\}\times A_0$ and lie over the map $g=\operatorname{pr}_B:\Delta^1\times B\to B$. Apply [lem-coef-infinity-equivalence-prism-extension] to $p=q$, $A=A_0$, $\epsilon=1$. Its inclusion contains every vertex, its vertical edges are the equivalences of Step 4, and $q$ is an inner fibration between quasicategories by Step 3. It gives $H_i:\Delta^1\times B\to E^\otimes$ exactly over $g$, with the specified terminal diagram and vertex edges. Let $s_i=H_i|_{\{0\}\times B}$ and $a_i:s_i\to s$ be this transformation over $B$. In particular $s_i(h_{AB})=\mathcal R_i(A,B)$ and $a_i(h_{AB})=e_i(A,B)$ exactly.

source.place: Proposition 4.4.5.8; all vertices, terminal endpoint and the varying operator simplex are fixed as required.

proof.text: The section $s_i$ preserves inert arrows. Let $u:\mathbf c\to\mathbf d$ be an inert operator; $s(u)$ is $q$-cocartesian because $s$ is inert-preserving. Every equivalence edge $e$ of $E^\otimes$ is $q$-cocartesian: a $\Lambda_0^n$ problem over $B$, $n\geq2$, with edge $01$ equal to $e$ has a filler by [lem-cbc-inner-fibration-equivalence-outer-horn-lift], which is the horn definition. By [lem-coef-infinity-mapping-composition] the equivalence $a_{i,\mathbf d}$ has an inverse $b$ with a $2$-simplex $\tau$ of edges $(a_{i,\mathbf d},b,1_{s_i(\mathbf d)})$, and $b$ is again an equivalence, hence $q$-cocartesian. The square $H_i|_{\Delta^1\times u}$ consists of two $2$-simplices with long edge $w:s_i(\mathbf c)\to s(\mathbf d)$: $\sigma$ with edges $(a_{i,\mathbf c},s(u),w)$ and $\rho$ with edges $(s_i(u),a_{i,\mathbf d},w)$. Applied to $\sigma$, [lem-coef-infinity-cocartesian-composition-initiality] makes $w$ $q$-cocartesian. In the quasicategory $E^\otimes$ fill the inner horn $\Lambda_1^3$ with faces $012=\rho$, $123=\tau$ and $013$ the degeneracy of $s_i(u)$ repeating its target; they agree on the edges $01=s_i(u)$, $12=a_{i,\mathbf d}$, $13=1_{s_i(\mathbf d)}$. The face $023$ has edges $(w,b,s_i(u))$ with $w,b$ cocartesian, so the same lemma makes $s_i(u)$ $q$-cocartesian. Thus $s_i$ is an algebra in the full inert-preserving section category of [def-coef-relative-symmetric-operadic-algebras].

source.place: Definition 2.1.3.1; inert-preservation of the transported section, since cocartesian edges are stable under composition with equivalence edges (HTT Propositions 2.4.1.5 and 2.4.1.7, through the cited nodes).

proof.text:
Extract operations from $s_i$ using [lem-coef-colored-operation-section-reconstruction]. Its transformation clause applied to $a_i$ gives compatibility of these operations with the original ones, including all substitution homotopies, because $H_i$ is defined on the whole operator nerve. For clarity, with $d_i$ an enriched inverse of $e_i$, the binary operation is equivalent to
$$m_i=d_i(A,C)\,m\,(e_i(B,C)\otimes e_i(A,B)),$$
the identity is $d_i(A,A)(\mathrm{id}_A)$, and evaluation is $\mathrm{ev}_i=\mathrm{ev}\,(e_i(A,B)\otimes1_A)$ up to the supplied coherent comparisons. These formulas follow by composing the operation-naturality square with $d_i$ and its inverse homotopy; the unary and empty-input cases are included. The higher compatibilities are the restrictions of the same $H_i$ to chains of operators, rather than independent choices inferred from these binary formulas.

source.place: Reconstruction with parameter Delta^1; explicit binary, nullary and evaluation identifications of the transported operation system.

proof.text: We check that $a_i$ is invertible in the category of sections over $B$, so that its inverse retains the operation coherences. Put $Q=\operatorname{Fun}(B,E^\otimes)$, $T=\operatorname{Fun}(B,B)$ and $p_Q=q_*$. These are quasicategories, and $p_Q$ is inner: a relative inner-horn problem transposes to a lifting problem for $q$ against $B\times\Lambda_j^n\hookrightarrow B\times\Delta^n$. This inclusion is inner anodyne by [lem-coef-inner-anodyne-pushout-product], using $\varnothing\hookrightarrow B$. The same argument for a map to the point gives the quasicategory assertions. Every vertex component of $a_i$ is an equivalence, so [lem-coef-infinity-pointwise-equivalences] makes $a_i$ an equivalence edge in $Q$. The strict fiber $S=p_Q^{-1}(\mathrm{id}_B)$ is a quasicategory: fill an inner horn by the inner-fibration property over the constant base simplex.

source.place: Relative diagram setup for Proposition 4.4.5.8; exponential inner-horn adjunction, followed by pointwise equivalence detection (Kerodon 01DK).

proof.text: In $Q$, prescribe a $\Lambda_0^2$ with vertices $(s_i,s,s_i)$, edges $01=a_i$, $02=1_{s_i}$, and constant base $\mathrm{id}_B$. The relative outer-horn theorem [lem-cbc-inner-fibration-equivalence-outer-horn-lift] for $p_Q$ gives a triangle over that constant base; call its edge $12=b_i:s\to s_i$. To obtain the other inverse triangle for this same $b_i$, prescribe $\Lambda_0^3$ with vertices $(s_i,s,s_i,s)$: face $012$ is that triangle, face $013$ is the degeneracy of $a_i$ repeating its target, and face $023$ is the degeneracy of $a_i$ repeating its source. The faces agree on their shared edges $01,02,03$. Their base is constant, and initial edge $a_i$ is an equivalence in $Q$. The same cited theorem fills this horn over that base. Face $123$ has consecutive edges $b_i,a_i$ and long edge $1_s$. Both inverse triangles therefore lie in $S$. By the relative-algebra definition the inert-preserving sections form a full subcategory of $S$. Its endpoints $s_i,s$ belong to it by Step 6, so $b_i$ and both triangles belong to it too. Thus $a_i$ is an algebra equivalence over $B$, and its inverse at a singleton hom color is an enriched inverse of $e_i(A,B)$.

source.place: Relative initial outer-horn lifting in dimensions 2 and 3; explicit inverse triangles over the identity diagram.

proof.text: In this same algebra category compose $s_1\xrightarrow{a_1}s\xrightarrow{b_2}s_2$. It is an equivalence, with inverse $b_1a_2$ and inverse homotopies obtained by composing those of Step 9. At each hom color its component is $d_2(A,B)e_1(A,B)$, where $d_2$ is the chosen enriched inverse from Step 9. At value colors it is equivalent to $1_A$: the inverse triangle for $a_2(v_A)=1_A$ identifies $b_2(v_A)$ with $1_A$. The transformation and parameter clauses of [lem-coef-colored-operation-section-reconstruction] identify this algebra equivalence with compatibility of composition, identities and evaluation, and every higher substitution comparison. If another inverse of $e_2$ is used to write $e_2^{-1}e_1$, its equivalence to $d_2$ is obtained by composing its unit with $d_2$ and the counit of $e_2$; whiskering this equivalence gives the same compatibility data up to coherent equivalence. No equality of strict dg operations is asserted.

source.place: Reconstruction with arbitrary parameter: composition of the two algebra equivalences and its singleton-color interpretation.

proof.text:
Finally $d_2e_1$ is a composite of enriched equivalences. By [lem-coef-dg-enrichment-rectification] and [lem-coef-enriched-category-tensor-calculus], these are fully faithful enriched functors, so for $x,y\in\mathcal R_1(A,B)$ the induced map
$$\mathcal R_1(A,B)(x,y)\longrightarrow\mathcal R_2(A,B)(d_2e_1x,d_2e_1y)$$
is an equivalence in $\mathbf D(\mathbf Z)$. The internal-Hom statement of the tensor-calculus node identifies these mapping objects with the derived transformation objects. In particular the conclusion retains the entire derived object, not just $H^0$. Steps 5–10 supply the transported operations and their model comparison, and this mapping-object equivalence gives the final clause.

source.place: Remark 9.5 and the mapping-object meaning of fully faithful enriched functors; Corollary 10.8 is consistent with this interpretation but is not used as a transport theorem.

proof_origin.place: Agent-written operadic transport proof: reconstruct the supplied operations as one section, extend the prescribed tuple equivalences by Kerodon 01NX, preserve inert edges by their mapping squares, and invert the transformation over the base using 01H0. Haugseng Remark 9.5 supplies the starting closed tensor through the existing node; the online references are unarchived (WANTED in report.md).
